items.title: Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Olayinka Ajayi Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused President Bola Tinubu of shifting responsibility for Nigeria’s economic hardship to the opposition, insisting that the administration must account for its record ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), was reacting to Tinubu’s remark at the APC campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday that the opposition created hunger and poverty in the country. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the President’s comment as “either delusion or a staggering case of political amnesia”. “The APC governed Nigeria for eight years before you took office. You have added another three and a half years. Nigerians know who has been in power, and hardship did not begin when the opposition started talking about it. Stop insulting their intelligence and answer for your record,” he said. Atiku accused Tinubu’s administration of worsening the hardship faced by Nigerians, arguing that the President could not dismiss concerns about the cost of living by blaming political opponents. He also criticised Tinubu’s planned inauguration of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, alleging that the ceremony showed how disconnected the President was from the daily realities of Nigerians. “A road cannot be completed with a speech or a ribbon cutting ceremony,” he said. The former Vice President challenged the administration to explain the removal of the petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the naira, which he claimed had fallen from about ₦471 to ₦1,329 to the dollar. He also cited a World Bank estimate that 63 per cent of Nigerians would be below the national poverty line in 2026, accusing the government of presiding over rising poverty. Atiku further questioned the extension of the 2024 budget into 2025 alongside a separate 2025 budget, as well as what he described as ₦7.13 trillion recorded under “energy security” in 2024 and ₦11.2 trillion in NNPC pipeline-related spending. The post Blaming opposition for hunger is delusional — Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu flags-off campaign, blasts opposition, backs APC governors against Rainbow Coalition
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu on Saturday opened the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna with a direct attack on his political opponents, accusing them of creating the hunger and poverty currently facing Nigerians, while asking supporters to mobilise for his re-election on January 16, 2027. Read Also: 2027: ‘They created the hunger’ — Tinubu slams opponents at Kaduna rally The President described the opposition as failures and angry people who rely on heckling instead of constructive policy, saying they have nothing to offer the country. Addressing the crowd at the campaign flag-off, Tinubu said: “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. They created the poverty we are trying to eradicate.” He defended his administration’s record, saying: “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing.” Tinubu told supporters that a second term would deliver “prosperity, continuity, progress and development,” adding: “To you, the children of our country, it is a promise of second-term prosperity. You will not regret going to vote.” He repeatedly asked the audience to confirm that they possessed their Permanent Voter Cards, saying: “Do you have your PVC? Do you have your PVC? Show your hands up.” The President also dismissed opposition criticism as anger arising from failure. “This is not a matter of hunger; this is not a matter of anger either. Our opponents are angry because they are failures. They have nothing to offer you but heckling,” he said. “We have prosperity, consistency, growth, recovery and opportunity. I assure you,” Tinubu declared. In apparent support of the APC governors’ position against the call by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, for a rainbow coalition, Tinubu urged voters to come out “massively” on January 16, 2027, to re-elect him and support APC candidates across the board. “Come January 2027, January 16, you must go out massively to elect me again. APC all the way. APC for our governors. APC for our senators. APC for our honourable members of the House of Representatives and all houses of assembly,” he said. He added: “Your prosperity is here. Your future is in your hands; the fingerprint will reflect it.” On the pledge by former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to bring back petrol subsidy if elected, Tinubu said the removal of fuel subsidy belonged to the past and pledged a future free of corruption and economic sabotage. “Fuel subsidy is in our past. No more corruption. No more falsification of invoices. No more lies. No more smuggling of wealth,” he said. He praised APC governors, saying: “Out of 36 of them, I can see the development strides they are making in their various states,” and reiterated his promise of “a better tomorrow.” The Kaduna rally marks the formal launch of the APC’s campaign for Tinubu’s re-election ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. He cautioned voters to remain vigilant against lies and ensure that their choices are accurately reflected through fingerprinting. President Tinubu acknowledged the historical significance of Kaduna State, where political leaders converged before independence. He offered prayers for the souls of departed leaders, asking God to forgive their sins and grant them peaceful repose. President Tinubu promised that voters would not regret supporting his re-election, under the pillars of growth, recovery and opportunity. Key corrections Speaking earlier, the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima said “Nigeria needs this finest servant to stand together.” According to him: “What we have done is to fight for the survival of this nation. So, allow me, Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, to reintroduce ourselves to you and show you that you do not have allies as sincere as we are. “We were able to keep this country together and defy the predictions of those who had predicted economic failure because we worked together. “Almost four years ago, you spoke eloquently, sincerely, boldly and decisively to elect a change-maker, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, as President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “We didn’t win that election because we were wise, far from it. We didn’t win that election because we were rich, and we didn’t win that election because we were educated. We didn’t win that election because we were the best speakers. We won because you saw the options before you and knew, without a doubt, that the alternative was a calamity.’’ “And for the good people of Kaduna State, we have seen why you, too, were told to renew the mandate of the APC and give His Excellency, Governor Uba Sani a mandate to redeem the fortunes of this great state. “His wisdom has made Kaduna State a unified place, where the man from Zonkwa sees the man from Zaria as a brother, and where the dividends of our democracy are felt in Kachia as they are in metropolitan Kaduna. “This is the legacy of the APC in Kaduna State. This is the mandate we have come to ask you to renew: a second term for the APC, from top to bottom.” Why Kaduna? On why Kaduna was chosen, the Vice President said: “We have the courage to come to Kaduna State today because we have kept our promise and never reneged on it. “First and foremost, we promised to restore the glory of Kaduna State as a national centre of learning. Did we deliver on that? We have brought you the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, haven’t we? We have carried forward the transition to the Federal University of Education, Zaria, haven’t we? “We have established state vocational institutes in Rigachikun, Soba and Samaru Kataf, with over 4,000 graduates. “We have committed all our education funding through NELFUND to support hundreds of thousands of students in universities, haven’t we? So, the APC is a party that delivers on its promises. “And you can bear witness that in 2015 and 2019, President Tinubu stood solidly behind the late President Muhammadu Buhari, securing his first- and second-term victories. “This is the reason why we have all stood with him to declare our support for Alhaji Bola Tinubu. This is a man of honour, a man of integrity and a man of honour.” Vanguard News The post Tinubu flags-off campaign, blasts opposition, backs APC governors against Rainbow Coalition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Decoding defence deals
items.description: SINCE September 2025, Pakistan has signed multilayered and multi-domain defence agreem­e­nts with several Arab and Muslim states. It has sig­­ned a Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement (SMDA) with Saudi Arabia, the Makkah Joint Def­­ence Agreement (MJDA) with Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, and a defence pact with Kuwait. Pak­istan has recently signed another defence agree­ment — the Badr agreement . Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia are signatories to this pact. These defence deals have, in the past year, increased Pakistan’s strategic relevance in the Middle East. Interestingly, each accord carries the explicit provision for joint defence production and investment in the defence industry. This clause in every defence pact reveals Islamabad’s long-term strategic objective of moving from a buyer-seller relationship to a co-production partnership with reliable partners in the region. There are four primary strategic factors that have driven Islamabad’s emphasis on the joint defence production clause in each defence pact. The India factor remains the primary driver. New Delhi’s defence budget now exceeds $80 billion, and its rapid induction of advanced platforms has widened the qualitative gap. Joint production arrangements with middle powers are likely to allow Pakistan to accelerate defence modernisation without bearing the full research and development cost. By manufacturing components and subsystems domestically, Pakistan can sustain a higher operational tempo and maintain credible conventional deterrence. Islamabad believes that strategic parity in South Asia does not require numerical equivalence. It primarily requires the ability to absorb, adapt, and indigenise technology at a pace that may prevent New Delhi from achieving decisive superiority over Islamabad. These defence deals, therefore, function as a force-multiplier for Pakis­tan’s conventional and strategic capabilities. Pakistan’s defence pacts over the past year have increased its strategic relevance. Islamabad’s second strategic objective is the diversification of defence suppliers and reduced reliance of its defence supply chain on Western weapons. Historically, Islamabad has relied on Chinese weapons but the extent of dependency has increased significantly in the last two decades. The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute has noted that this dependency is nearly 80 per cent. Although Pakistan and China enjoy unprecedented trust and depth in their all-weather strategic relationship, in theoretical terms, heavy reliance on any single external source worries Islamabad. Similarly, Islamabad is increasingly seeking to decouple its military procurement from Western-reliant supply chains. This approach is rooted in Pakistan’s historically bitter experiences with sudden embargoes and sanctions, alongside Islamabad’s broader resistance to the West’s tendency to use defence exports as political leverage over the Global South during geopolitical crises. Primarily, Islamabad is eager to cultivate robu­­st, non-Western defence partnerships to secure reliable and uninterrupted arms supplies free from the influence of foreign powers. By integrating affluent Saudi and Qatari capital with the technologically advanced Turkish weapons industry, Pakistan is building an insulated, collaborative defence network with the middle powers to achieve this strategic objective. Islamabad belie­ves that these defence deals, alongside its strategic alliance with China, may allow Islamabad to minimise its conventional vulnerabilities, help mod­­ernise its armed forces, and ultimately achieve a much higher degree of long-term strategic autonomy. Moreover, Islamabad is acutely aware that the intensifying US-China strategic competition will make it increasingly difficult to maintain a purely China-centric defence supply chain in the long run. Therefore, by building parallel defence production partnerships with Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkiye, and Indonesia, Pakistan is creating a middle-power buffer to avoid unwanted political pressure from the US. Interestingly, these countries are not fully aligned with either Washington or Beijing, and provide Islamabad greater room for manoeuvre. Third, the economic factor equally occupies the strategic motivations of Islamabad. Pakistan wants to enhance its ability to modernise the defence production industry and increase defence exports. Pakistan’s official defence exports stood at approximately $280m in 2024. The recently concluded deals can significantly enhance defence exports to $650-700m by 2027, crossing the $1bn mark by 2030. The Gulf states, seeking to reduce their own dependence on Western suppliers, constitute the most immediate and lucrative market for Pakistani defence exports. Joint ventures under the Badr agreement, MJDA and SMDA are designed to produce systems that meet the Gulf’s operational requirements, while carrying Pakistani certification, and, crucially, a lower price tag. Successful penetration of these markets would generate much-needed foreign exchange for Pakistan, create skilled employment, and justify further capital investment in the domestic defence industry. Beyond the Gulf, there is also potential for niche exports to African and Central Asian countries that face similar budgetary constraints and seek cost-effective, reliable platforms. The fourth objective linked to the third is to attract foreign direct investment to Pakistan’s defence sector. The joint production clauses are structured to encourage equity participation rather than simple technology licensing. Early commitments already indicate potential inflows of $1.2-1.5bn over the next five years in manufacturing facilities, testing ranges, and human capital development. These investments will upgrade the physical infrastructure of Pakistan’s public-sector defence industry. These inflows can stimulate related industries, including electronics, metallurgy, and software, while creating thousands of high-skill jobs for individuals who would otherwise migrate overseas. Time will tell whether these defence deals can deliver a meaningful technology transfer. The most important question is whether such a multipronged approach can genuinely enhance Pakis­tan’s long-term strategic autonomy or will merely redistribute its dependencies. It is also unclear to what extent these defence deals can genuinely reduce Pakistan’s strategic vulnerabilities. However, despite these uncertainties, these defence deals will bring critical capital and technical know-how, while reducing vulnerability to external supply shocks. Yet Islamabad must calibrate its exposure with precision. Over-commitment in the complex security theatres of the Middle East can risk entangling Pakistan in conflicts whose political and military logic lies beyond Islamabad’s core interests. Therefore, Pakistan must pursue these opportunities with strategic clarity and within well-defined red lines. The writer is a strategic analyst of international security. The views expressed are his own. X: @itskhurramabbas Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan export initiative
items.description: DOES any such initiative exist in our country, or is it a figment of my imagination? For sure, there is an initiative for remittances — but not for exports. One wonders about the presence of one and the strange absence of the other. Exports are stagnating, and remittances are rising . Are exports falling because of unwise policies or despite them? Are remittances rising because of good policy initiatives or despite them? The point here is not to denigrate the remittances initiative or its continually renewed push, but to emphasise that exports should be given greater policy priority than remittances — because, in some growth-promoting way, exports matter far more than remittances. Here we explore the reasons. This article focuses on increasing exports, not reducing remittances. In fact, remittances should continue to be promoted. Both exports and remittances matter to our economy. Both help contain the current account deficit. Exports are driven by agricultural, industrial, and services output — sectors that already provide a direct impetus to employment in the country. This impetus also has an indirect impact on the economy through spending by household members employed in export industries. Remittances follow increased output in foreign countries that employ Pakistani workers and pay them abroad. Part of their overseas earnings/ savings is sent home to their families. The economic impact of remittances is indirect and arises from spending by remittance-receiving families. Hence, both help fill the gap in the current account, but the growth impact of exports is both direct and indirect, while it is only indirect for remittances. Another, far more crucial point is that increasing exports to raise the economy’s productivity is paramount for growth. This is not true for rising remittances in Pakistan, although it is theoretically possible if a larger proportion of remittances goes towards export production. Our policymakers seem to have forgotten the importance of exports. A policy to increase exports is more likely to raise productivity than a policy to increase remittances. Increased productivity can fuel long-term sustainable growth. Exporting exposes domestic firms to international competition, better management practices, international quality standards, global supply chains, and new technologies. There is considerable empirical evidence that exporters tend to be more productive and that export expansion can generate productivity gains. For example, the World Bank reports that a 10 per cent increase in exports across its cross-country sample was associated with higher employment, earnings, and productivity. Another point to note is that exports are always preceded by the actual rise in production and employment (direct impact), as well as the indirect impact through consumption made possible by spending of wages by export-related employees. Contrast this with remittances, whose economic impact is not only indirect but also follows the receipt of remittances. This means that prioritising sustained export growth would create more employment in the country and reduce the desperation of unemployed people pushed abroad to find jobs, even at the risk of their lives. At the same time, increasing exports would have boosted the productivity our economy so badly needs. This is why remittances should not be seen as a substitute for exports. Exports should be promoted with more vigour than remittances. In terms of promoting growth, exports matter far more than remittances. Our analysts tend to blame high unemployment almost entirely on high population growth. The fact is that our unwise economic policies are at the root of frequent economic crises that cause growth and productivity to decline. The resulting rise in joblessness leads to greater migration abroad, which, in turn, drives remittances up. Of course, Pakistan’s remittance initiative has helped. But if we had implemented prudent policies that avoided various crises, exports as a proportion of GDP would have risen much faster than remittances. The export-to-GDP ratio peaked at 17.3pc in 1992 (according to World Bank data). It went down to only 10pc of GDP in 2025. The trajectory of the fall was not linear. Every onslaught of a balance-of-payments crisis precipitated a large decline. It fell to 9.6pc of GDP in 2000 in the wake of the 1998-99 crisis. With more prudent policies after the crisis, it recovered somewhat — only to decline again when imprudent policies followed, leading to other crises between 2000 and now. In contrast, our remittances have been rising almost consistently during this period as a proportion of GDP. Remittances dipped from 3.2pc of GDP in 1992 to 1.1pc of GDP in 2000, then rose to 9.9pc. The presence of a falling trend in exports and a rising trend in remittances indicates that exports always respond positively to prudent economic policies, while remittances largely show autonomous growth. Refinements in the banking infrastructure have indeed helped to increase remittances, but economic policies also played a role that pushed people into boats to find employment abroad. Subsequent remittance growth has largely occurred despite these economic policies. Pakistan’s export potential is much higher than its current level suggests. The simplest way to estimate what the level of exports could have been in 2026 is to assume the export-to-GDP ratio of 1992 (17.3pc). This translates to exports valued at $78bn, compared with the actual export value of $41bn (FY26 State Bank data). Frequent balance-of-payments crises in our country seem to have clouded the thinking of our policymakers. When they think about exports or remittances or even foreign investment, they only think in terms of foreign exchange earnings or inflows that fill a gap in the balance-of-payments. Constant firefighting and pressing short- and mid-term foreign financing needs have created a policy psyche that is obsessed with mobilising foreign exchange liquidity and has forgotten productivity and growth. Exports are badly in need of an initiative based on collective policy expertise in the country. The writer is a former deputy governor of the State Bank of Pakistan. rriazuddin@gmail.com Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan's trade gap with Gulf partners narrows
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s trade deficit with Gulf partner countries narrowed 26.35 per cent to $2.85bn in the first quarter of 2026-27 against $3.87bn a year earlier, largely due to lower imports and moderately higher exports. The steepest declines were 97.46pc and 72.51pc in import payments to Kuwait and Qatar. These two countries accounted for $947.923 million of the gross decline in import payments, partly offset by the substantial increase in imports from Oman. On the export side, the UAE accounted for approximately 66.21pc of Pakistan’s total exports to the seven countries in 1QFY27, followed by Saudi Arabia at 19.45pc. The remaining five countries collectively accounted for just 14.34pc, according to data compiled by the State Bank of Pakistan. The Middle East conflict has disrupted Pakistan’s trade since March. Exports to most Gulf states are shrinking, while imports from them are surging—worsening Pakistan’s external vulnerability and dependence on Gulf energy and raw materials. Lower imports, higher exports cut gap by 26pc to $2.85bn in July-September September emerged as the sixth month after the March contraction, suggesting Pakistan’s import flows are highly sensitive to geopolitical developments, particularly in energy corridors. Pakistan remained heavily reliant on energy imports, particularly from the UAE and Saudi Arabia, which accounted for 90pc combined. Other countries, including Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Jordan and Bahrain, remain secondary contributors despite their export capacity. Pakistan’s exports to the Middle East rose 10.96pc to $864.878m in 1QFY27, up from $779.425m in the same period last year. In FY26, exports to the region fell by over 2pc to $3.093bn from $3.152bn the previous year. In contrast, imports from the region fell 20.02pc to $3.717bn in 1QFY27, down from $4.648bn a year earlier. In FY26, imports posted negative growth of 4pc to $16.413bn from $17.097bn a year earlier. Country-wide data showed exports to Saudi Arabia grew by 4.92pc in 1QFY27 from a year ago. Imports, however, dipped by 18.52pc from Saudi Arabia, showing a clear dip in Pakistan’s imports of Saudi goods, especially oil. A positive trend was observed in export proceeds to the UAE, which increased by 16.35pc in 3MFY27, with notable gains in Abu Dhabi, Ajman, and Fujairah. Imports from the UAE fell by 6.15pc, mainly due to lower petroleum and commodity inflows. Exports to Qatar fell by nearly 22.79pc, while imports dipped by 72.51pc in 1QFY27 year on year. The import decline reflects a major reversal in energy-related purchases from the region. Exports to Kuwait dipped 2.24pc, but imports plunged 97.46pc in 1QFY27. This indicates Pakistan’s reliance on Kuwaiti imports, especially petroleum, compared to a year ago. Exports to Bahrain contracted 23.07pc, while imports also dipped 17.31pc in 1QFY27. Exports to Jordan rose by 4.70pc, while imports declined 29.27pc. Pakistan’s exports to Oman rose 10.73pc while imports surged 97.40pc during July-September. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Prudent warning
items.description: AS speculation grows regarding fresh US-Israeli aggression against Iran, major Muslim states of the wider Middle East, as well as European powers, have clearly expressed their lack of appetite for any such misadventure. Meeting in Istanbul on Friday under the ‘R4+E3’ umbrella, the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkiye, the UK, Germany, and France discussed several global hotspots, including Iran and Ukraine. Italy also participated in the meeting. The Turkish foreign minister said that “no one supports” military intervention in Iran at this moment, while France’s top diplomat said any escalation “would only have losers”, besides increasing oil prices, which are already high. There is good reason for the international community to be worried. Strong signals are emerging from Tel Aviv and Washington that the US and Israel are planning a new assault on Iran, reportedly after the American midterms on Nov 3 — perhaps even earlier. US President Donald Trump has himself said that “we may do another little Epic Fury”, referring to the name America gave to the aggression launched in February. While the US leader is known for his bluster and often non-serious threats, in this regard he may actually mean what he has said. The US has been sending more troops and military equipment to the Middle East, and American and Israeli forces have reportedly rehearsed attack plans. Tel Aviv is particularly enthused about going after Iran again. Doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results each time is equated with folly. But arrogance has blinded both the US and Israel to this reality. Israel had first attacked Iran in October 2024, while both the US and the Zionist state initiated two more aggressive operations against the Islamic Republic, in June 2025 and February 2026. These attacks, particularly the assault launched this year, inflicted huge damage on Iran, decimating its military, political, and religious leadership. But the country regrouped, defended itself, and fought back against the aggressors. The Iranians have reaffirmed that any new attack will be met with “offensive” measures. All of this is cause for alarm. The Gulf states that host American facilities will again be in the line of fire, which is why Muslim countries have warned against a new conflict. But will the war lobbies in Washington and Tel Aviv listen? Many governments and most people of the Middle East are tired of war, and want to rebuild their lives and economies. If conflict and bloodshed return, the shockwaves caused by disrupted energy and trade flows will leave few economies unscathed. Therefore, America should abandon its plans to further destabilise the region. Instead, it should rein in its ally Israel and its bloodthirsty leaders. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
items.description: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said. After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France’s modern history. The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000. Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched. President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days. Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city’s Porte d’Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism. Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that “several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters”, the AFP news agency reported. In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France’s second-largest city. Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux. In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture. “There were around 150 of us, mostly secondary school and university students. Then the tear gas came almost immediately. You could barely see anything in the street,” said one protester in France’s third-largest city. Nuñez said late in the day that nearly 1,000 people had been arrested, a number he said would increase. The minister also said two people had been “seriously injured”: one in the south-western city of Toulouse, and another one in Clermont-Ferrand, central France. Earlier, a peaceful protester in Paris who gave her name as Zelie told the BBC people had taken to the streets because they were “really frustrated” and had been “suffering a lot” since Macron came to office. “They keep us quiet. They take our money, they tax us a lot and we can’t say anything. Today we are in the streets because it’s been too long, it’s been too much,” the 26-year-old said. Two masked teenage protesters, who did not want to give their names, also said their generation was in despair and felt abandoned by the government. “I think looting is really not good,” one of the demonstrators said of last Saturday’s disorder. “But it’s because of poverty and the violence of the police.” He added that the protests would end “when we have a response to our demands. We really want a change in France”. Meanwhile, some 13,000 people joined a rally against the hard-right National Rally party in the north-central city of Orléans which proceeded peacefully. Mass protests triggered by similar issues as in France also rocked several other European cities on Saturday. In Albania’s capital Tirana, riot police fired tear gas to disperse thousands of anti-government demonstrators, while clashes were also reported in Belgium’s capital Brussels. In Milan, northern Italy, a major security operation including hundreds of soldiers alongside police prevented protesters gathering in the city. Many had feared a repeat of violent scenes last week when some started fires, smashed windows and looted shops.

items.title: Mali: plus de 4.880 combattants neutralisés en près de six mois
items.description: Les Forces armées maliennes (FAMa) ont annoncé avoir neutralisé plus de 4.880 combattants de groupes armés et détruit 162 bases entre mai et le 20 octobre 2026, dans le cadre de leurs opérations de sécurisation du territoire, rapportent des médias locaux. Ce bilan, présenté vendredi par la Direction de l'information et des relations publiques des Armées (DIRPA), fait également état de la destruction de 315 véhicules de type pick-up et d'environ 1.300 motocyclettes, précisent les mêmes sources. Les opérations militaires ont notamment porté sur la consolidation des positions militaires dans la région de Kidal au nord du pays, et la sécurisation des corridors d'approvisionnement. Selon la DIRPA, l'armée a effectué 1.887 missions aériennes de surveillance et de suivi entre mai et septembre, ainsi que 791 frappes aériennes, ajoutant que soixante-cinq autres frappes ont été menées entre le 1er et le 20 octobre. Dans le nord du Mali, les opérations ont principalement concerné les régions de Gao, Ménaka et Kidal, où les forces gouvernementales ont repris position au début du mois d'octobre, à la suite d'une offensive lancée le 6 octobre. Une mission du chef d'État-major général des Armées, effectuée les 10 et 11 octobre, a notamment porté sur les conditions du retour progressif des populations, de l'administration et des services sociaux de base dans cette zone. Dans le centre du pays, les opérations récentes ont permis, selon le commandement militaire, de neutraliser plus de 200 combattants et de détruire dix véhicules et 95 motocyclettes. Par ailleurs, l'armée malienne a renforcé la sécurisation des axes routiers afin de faciliter l'acheminement des produits de première nécessité, notamment les hydrocarbures, vers les principaux centres urbains. Dans ce cadre, la DIRPA a fait état de l'escorte de 2.556 camions-citernes en septembre sur l'axe Kadiana-Bamako, contre 3.681 camions-citernes accompagnés sur différents axes en août. Les autorités militaires poursuivent également le renforcement des effectifs des FAMa, à travers l'intégration de nouvelles recrues et de jeunes issus du Service national des jeunes. Le Mali demeure confronté à l'activité de plusieurs groupes armés, notamment dans ses régions septentrionales et centrales, malgré la multiplication des opérations militaires et des dispositifs de sécurisation des axes d'approvisionnement. The post Mali: plus de 4.880 combattants neutralisés en près de six mois appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tinubu blames opposition for hunger, poverty in Nigeria; Atiku kicks, says president delusional
items.description: President Bola Tinubu has accused opposition politicians of causing the hunger and poverty Nigerians are experiencing, insisting that his administration is working to address the problems as he formally launched his 2027 presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday. Mr Tinubu made the remarks at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off at Ranchers Bees Stadium (also known as Kaduna Township Stadium), ahead of the 2027 general elections. I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who caused them? They did! They caused hunger and poverty. We are trying to eliminate them,” the president said. He also urged his supporters to be wary of statements from the opposition, particularly criticism of his decision to remove the petrol subsidy, insisting that the country would not return to the previous system. “Be careful; watch them. Don’t let them lie to you. What is past is in the past. “Fuel subsidy is in our past: no more corruption, no more falsification of invoices, no more lies, no more smuggling of fuel,” Mr Tinubu told supporters at the rally. The president’s remarks come amid persistent public concerns over high food prices, inflation and declining purchasing power, issues expected to feature prominently in political debates ahead of the 2027 elections. In a swift reaction to the president’s remarks, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, described President Tinubu’s claim “as a delusional, shameless attempt to dodge responsibility for the misery his own government has inflicted on Nigerians.” He said a president cannot light the fire of hardship with his own policies, then blame the neighbours for the smoke. Tinubu defends petrol subsidy removal Since assuming office in May 2023, the Tinubu administration has implemented major economic reforms, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign exchange regime. The government has defended the measures as necessary to reduce public expenditure, tackle alleged corruption associated with the subsidy system and establish the foundations for sustainable economic growth. While Mr Tinubu insists that the removal of the subsidy is irreversible, critics continue to demand evidence that the savings and additional revenue generated by the reforms are translating into improved living conditions for ordinary Nigerians. At the rally, the president also said salaries were being paid on time and praised APC governors for their development projects. Tinubu thanks Kaduna residents At the rally, Mr Tinubu thanked the people of Kaduna State for supporting him in the 2023 presidential election, saying their backing contributed to his victory. “You gave me the joy of remembering the victory you gave me to become president. I have returned to thank you once again,” he said. He urged Nigerians to give him another opportunity in 2027, promising to continue pursuing his agenda of prosperity, development and national growth. Tinubu has a long history of supporting the North – VP Shettima Vice President Kashim Shettima defended Mr Tinubu’s political relationship with northern Nigeria, saying the president had supported politicians from the region for years, including those who contested the presidency in previous elections. Mr Shettima cited Mr Tinubu’s political relationships with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the late President Muhammadu Buhari to argue that the president had consistently supported northern political figures. “President Bola Tinubu is one person who has fiercely identified with the North over the years. It is pertinent to mention that when former Vice President Atiku Abubakar was harassed and chased off the PDP with his tail between his legs, he ran to the Lion of Bourdillon, who gave him political succour, support and a platform to contest for the presidency of this country in 2007. “In 2011, Asiwaju supported another northerner, Nuhu Ribadu, and in 2015 and 2019, he supported our late President Muhammadu Buhari,” Mr Shettima said. The expression, “Lion of Bourdillon,” refers to Mr Tinubu, whose residence on Bourdillon Road in Lagos has become associated with his political influence. Atiku contested the presidency under the Action Congress (AC) in 2007 after leaving the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with support from Mr Tinubu and other party leaders. In 2011, Mr Ribadu contested the presidency under the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), a party led by Mr Tinubu. In 2015 and 2019, Mr Tinubu supported Mr Buhari’s presidential bids under the APC. However, Mr Tinubu and Atiku subsequently became political opponents, particularly during the 2019 and 2023 presidential elections, when the former vice president contested under the PDP while Mr Tinubu was in the APC. Mr Shettima’s remarks were part of the APC’s effort to highlight Mr Tinubu’s history of political alliances and support for politicians from Northern Nigeria as the party seeks another presidential term for him in 2027. Top government officials attend the rally The event attracted senior federal government officials, APC governors and party leaders from different parts of the country. Those in attendance included Vice President Kashim Shettima and Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani, who received Mr Tinubu upon his arrival in the state. Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume was also among the senior officials at the event. Other attendees included ministers, senators, members of the House of Representatives, APC governors and prominent party figures. APC National Chairman Nentawe Yilwatda and Abdulaziz Yari, director-general of the party’s presidential campaign council, were among the party leaders involved in preparations for the rally and efforts to mobilise support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election. The event marked the official launch of the APC’s presidential campaign, as the party seeks to consolidate its support base ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.title: Obama attacks Trump as he campaigns for Democrats ahead of midterm elections
items.description: Former President Barack Obama has attacked the Trump administration over the Iran war and high consumer prices as he hit the campaign trail for Democrats ahead of the US midterm elections. “This election is our last best chance to at least rein in some of the foolishness of this administration,” Obama told crowds in Ohio on Saturday. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump touted his administration’s immigration and tariff policies at a rally in Georgia, telling supporters “we’re in the golden age of America”. The midterm elections on 3 November will decide which party controls Congress for the rest of Trump’s term, and therefore how easy it is for the president to carry out his plans. Early voting has already begun and Trump cast his ballot on Saturday in Florida alongside his wife First Lady Melania Trump. Speaking on Saturday in Ohio and Michigan, Obama targeted Trump and his cabinet members, at one point mocking the president’s attempt to redecorate the White House. “After two years of chaos and cruelty and corruption and incompetence, the likes of which we have not seen in the modern era, you get a chance to say, ‘enough is enough,'” the former president said in Cleveland. Obama said he sympathised with voters who rejected Democrats in 2024 over economic and inflation concerns following the Covid pandemic. But he said Trump had only himself to blame for the current state of the economy. “If you thought everything was too expensive before ‘you know who’,” he said, referring to Trump without using his name, “everything is more expensive now”. Trump, meanwhile, acknowledged that oil prices were “temporarily high” but said “our country is getting stronger and stronger all the time, and those pump prices are going to come down”. The Republican president has faced significant pressure to lower fuel prices, which have jumped due to the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Talking up the economy, Trump told the crowd in Perry “we’re taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs”, and repeated his pledge to offer every adult American a $5,000 (£3,700) payout if Republicans win both chambers of Congress. He also took aim at the Democrats, telling the crowd they would “loot your wealth” and “annihilate your borders”. Using derogatory language, he accused the Democrats of trying to open up immigration from Libya, Yemen, Haiti and Somalia – countries which he described as “terror-infested”. Describing a previous meeting with several senators, he recalled: “I said, ‘Why do we always have to take people from shithouse countries? Why can’t we take people from, like, well… Norway, Sweden? Why not Denmark?'”

items.title: ATC warns Imaan, husband of verdict sans testimony
items.description: • Couple refuses to record statements under Section 342 of CrPC; judge directs them to respond at next hearing on Monday • Defence seeks delay in verdict pending IHC ruling on transfer plea ISLAMABAD: While offering yet another opportunity to human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Hazir-Mazari and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha to record their statements in a security breach case, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday warned them that a verdict could come even without their testimony if they refused. ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra, who conducted the proceedings at Adiala jail, issued the warning after both accused declined to record their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) during Saturday’s hearing. The judge directed the couple to record their statements at the next hearing and adjourned the case until Monday, Oct 26. During Saturday’s proceedings, Hadi requested the court, “Let the state counsel record the statement under Section 342 on our behalf.” However, the judge replied that recording statements under Section 342 was a matter between the court and the accused, adding that they would have to respond themselves. “We will not record the statement under Section 342,” Ms Mazari stated. The judge warned that if the accused did not comply, the court would mention in its order that no response had been submitted. Ms Mazari and Mr Chattha are facing a jail trial in a 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. At the last hearing, a state-app­ointed counsel had cross-examined all prosecution witnesses. The court appointed Atif Mehmood as the state counsel to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses, replacing Taimoor Janjua, who was dismissed from the case over his past conduct. The court had ruled to appoint the state attorney after the defence counsel failed to cross-examine the prosecution witnesses. Separately, the defence filed an application requesting the trial court to refrain from delivering a final judgement until the Islamabad High Court decided a petition seeking the transfer of the case to another court. The application stated that the transfer petition was already pending before the IHC and requested that this development be made part of the trial court’s judicial record. The defence also pointed out that the appointment of the state counsel had been challenged before the IHC. The application urged the trial court to defer its final decision until the high court ruled on the transfer petition. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Wapda inks Rs133bn deal for Diamer-Bhasha Dam project
items.description: LAHORE: The Pakistan Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) signed an agreement on Saturday with the Power China-IKAN Joint Venture for the Rs133.18 billion hydro-mechanical (HM-1) contract for the Diamer-Bhasha Dam project. According to a Wapda spokesperson, the agreement was signed at Wapda House by Diamer-Bhasha Dam Project Chief Engineer and Project Director Arif Ali on behalf of the authority and Ling Jianke, the authorised representative of the joint venture. Wapda Chairman retired Lt Gen Muhammad Saeed, the authority’s members for finance, water and power, the chief executive officer of the Diamer-Bhasha Development Company, a delegation from the joint venture led by Power China International Group Limited chairman, and representatives of the consultants also attended the ceremony. The HM-1 contract covers the project’s hydro-mechanical equipment and hydraulic steel structures. The work includes the manufacture, supply and installation of gates and steel structures to control water flows at the dam. The equipment will be inst­alled at the flushing tunnels on both banks, the power intakes and the dam outlets. The contract also covers steel lining, hoisting and pumping systems, and related electrical works. The spokesperson said the Diamer-Bhasha Dam was a priority project of the federal government for ensuring the country’s water, food and energy security. The dam is being built across the Indus River, 40km downstream of Chilas. Upon completion, it will have a gross water storage capacity of 8.1 million acre-feet and an installed power generation capacity of 4,500 megawatts. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Indian Punjab CM wants to attend Lahore moot
items.description: • Bhagwant Mann says World Punjabi Conference organisers invited him; doubts BJP-led government will let him visit • Speaker Sandhwan jokes, ‘If you get permission, take us along as well’ INDIAN Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann expressed desire on Friday to attend the World Punjabi Conference in Lahore, claiming he had received an invitation, while taking a jab at the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over whether it would allow him to visit Pakistan, according to a BBC report. The 4th International Punjabi Confer­e­nce is scheduled for Nov 27-29 in Lahore. Mann made the remarks while addressing the Indian Punjab assembly. “They do not even let me go to France or Japan. How will they let me go to Pakistan?” he said, in a jibe at the BJP-led government in Delhi. In a video posted on his official YouTube channel, Mann said many poets from Indian Punjab would travel to the conference. “I also want to go, because our roots are one, our problems are also similar,” he said. The CM mentioned the invitation after reciting verses by Pakistani Punjabi poet Tajammul Kaleem. He said he had spoken to Pakistani Punjabi poet, Baba Najmi and received the invitation, adding that people on both sides of the border shared a culture and should interact. Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan replied, “If you get permission, take us along as well.” At this, voices of some other members also rose from within the house, endorsing what the speaker said. Mann also demanded the reopening of the Kartarpur corridor, sacred to Sikhs. Ties between India and Pakistan have been extremely strained since a four-day battle last year, with limited trade and diplomatic contact. Social media users in both countries called Mann’s wish pleasant despite the chill, according to BBC . Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Luv FM journalists sweep top honours at GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards
items.description: Journalists from Luv FM, a subsidiary of the Multimedia Group Limited, have won multiple awards at the 2025 Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards. Four journalists from the Kumasi-based station received honours across several categories, with Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe taking the night’s top prize as Ashanti Regional Journalist of the Year. Mr Quaicoe also won Best Feature Production, Best Agriculture Reporter, and placed second in Best Entertainment Journalism. Emmanuel Bright Quaicoe Clinton Yeboah secured first place in both Best Health Journalism and Best Business and Economy Journalism. Clinton Yeboah Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom won first place in Best Community Impact Journalism, placed second in Best Health Journalism and finished third in Best Environment, Science and Climate Journalism. Nana Boakye Dankwah Yiadom Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen also swept awards, including Best Science, Climate and Environment Reporter, and placed third in the Best Feature Production Category The awards recognise journalistic work across different beats, including health, business, entertainment, environmental reporting and community impact. Mr Quaicoe’s overall regional award, alongside the category wins secured by his colleagues, highlights the range of reporting represented by the Luv FM team. The GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards celebrate journalists whose work contributes to public understanding of issues affecting communities across the region. Luv FM, based in Kumasi, is part of the Multimedia Group’s network of radio and television stations in Ghana. The regional winners are expected to feature in the broader national awards calendar, although their participation and final standings at the national level will depend on the applicable GJA arrangements.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition forces, Houthis trade blows; 16 dead in Sanaa, Hodeida
items.description: • Houthi media says air raids leave casualties in Sanaa, Hodeida and Mocha • Rebel group claims strikes on Aden, airports, oil installations; Washington warns travellers • Falling debris reported near Makkah, Madina; Two ballistic missiles intercepted en route to Taif, Yanbu RIYADH: Saudi-led coalition forces launched deadly airstrikes on Yemen’s Houthi-controlled capital of Sanaa and the Red Sea port city of Hodeida on Saturday, killing at least 16 people, according to Houthi media. In response, the Houthi forces launched their own attacks targeting Saudi oil facilities, airports and military sites in the southern Yemeni city of Aden. The Houthis’ Al-Masirah television channel reported a series of “Saudi enemy airstrikes” targeting Sanaa and its surrounding governorate, while also reporting around 20 strikes on Mocha. In Sanaa, one strike hit a house, killing at least four people and wounding several others. A separate strike on a residential building for cement factory workers in the Sanaa governorate killed six women and one child and wounded three others, the broadcaster said. In the western port city of Hodeida, Al-Masirah reported that a Saudi strike killed five members of the same family. “Five people, the head of the family, two of his children and his two wives, have been martyred, and his daughter wounded, as a result of a Saudi enemy air strike on the home of citizen Abdulwahed al-Wasabi in the Al-Tuhayta district,” the channel reported. Earlier on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition announced it had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis toward the western Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu. Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence Agency briefly broadcast warnings of “potential danger” for four western regions, including Taif, Yanbu, Jeddah and Makkah, home to Islam’s holiest city. Residents were instructed to “proceed to the nearest safe place,” and the agency repeated a legal warning against sharing images or information related to “countering missiles and drones.” The alerts were rescinded about 10 minutes later after the agency said the threat had passed. In a post on X, the agency said it responded to falling debris following the interceptions in the Makkah and Madina areas. “Civil defence in the Makkah and Madina regions began to respond to the falling debris from the interception of two ballistic missiles launched by Houthis,” the agency said, adding that some shrapnel fell in Wadi Mughamas outside Makkah. Following the Saudi strikes, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group launched wide-scale attacks targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait. Saree added that Houthi forces targeted an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh oil refinery, crude oil pumping stations and the East-West Pipeline. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities on those reported strikes. On another front, explosions rocked Aden, the interim seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government. Yemen’s Interior Ministry told the state-run Saba news agency that three Houthi ballistic missiles struck coast guard sites, with two hitting the coast guard headquarters and a third striking a building in the Tawahi district. A police source added that a coalition position near the Aden airport was also targeted. Saree quickly claimed the Aden attack, saying Saudi officers were overseeing mobilisation there. “Our armed forces targeted Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden,” Saree said. US updates advisory On Saturday, the US Embassy in Riyadh and the US Mission to the United Arab Emirates stated that Washington’s travel advisories were updated to reflect an increase in potential armed attacks by the Houthis. Meanwhile, Egypt has suggested sending troops to help defend Saudi Arabia, while Britain and France have offered forces to protect the kingdom. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Gabd border crossing with Iran reopened
items.description: GWADAR: Pakistan reopened its border crossing with Iran at Gabd-Rimdan on Saturday, restoring bilateral trade and allowing stranded trucks carrying LPG and essential food commodities to resume movement after a weeklong suspension that began on Oct 17. Border officials cleared commercial consignments holding a consignment note dated Oct 16 or earlier to cross at the Gabd-Rimdan point, known as Gate 250, in Gwadar. Mir Naveed Jan Kalmati, president of the Gwadar Chamber of Commerce and Industry, confirmed that trade operations resumed on Saturday morning. “Pakistan has opened the border with Iran at Gabd-Rimdan this morning and allowed trucks and other vehicles to move toward Iran and Pakistan with import and export goods,” Kalmati said. Kalmati welcomed the decision, noting that the resumption of cross-border commerce will bring immediate relief to traders and transporters stranded on both sides. He added that the restored supply chain is expected to ease a nationwide LPG shortage and reduce soaring energy and food prices across Pakistan. Saturday’s reopening came after local administrators reviewed the security situation and deployed additional forces to protect trade convoys following an attack earlier in the week. On Thursday, unidentified gunmen had targeted the backlog of freight vehicles parked near the closed Gabd-Rimdan crossing, setting dozens of trucks ablaze and damaging several others. Those trucks had been stranded since Oct 17, when Pakistan’s Ministry of Commerce abruptly suspended trade at both the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings. The ministry issued a memorandum withdrawing an Oct 3 trade order with immediate effect without specifying a reason for the halt. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Dar orders urgent action to rein in rising wheat prices
items.description: • Calls for increased market supply, warns against hoarding and speculation • PTI Kisan Wing welcomes wheat support price, seeks effective procurement mechanism ISLAMABAD: Expressing concern over rising wheat prices, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Saturday directed federal and provincial governments to take all necessary measures, including increasing market supply, to bring prices under control. Chairing a cabinet committee meeting to review the stocks, prices and supply of essential commodities, Mr Dar emphasised that safeguarding national food security and ensuring the availability of essential items at reasonable prices were government priorities. The participants reviewed national reserves, procurement frameworks, domestic consumption and price trends. They were informed that stocks of essential commodities remained adequate, ensuring stability in local supplies. The committee was briefed that domestic and imported wheat stocks were sufficient to meet requirements until the next harvest. Regarding sugar, the committee was informed that its price in the domestic market remained well below the targeted retail price of Rs155 per kg, with surplus stocks available until the next crushing season. Mr Dar directed federal and provincial authorities to closely monitor market networks, stressing that all organisations must show zero tolerance for hoarding and market speculation. The meeting was attended by National Food Security and Research Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain, Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, the secretaries of the national food security and research and commerce ministries, the chief secretaries of all provinces, and senior officials from relevant federal and provincial departments. Implementation urged In a related development, the PTI Kisan Wing has welcomed the government’s announcement of a wheat support price of Rs4,500 per maund (40kg), while expressing reservations about its implementation and demanding concrete measures to ensure farmers receive the announced rate for their produce. A day earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif set the new indicative wheat support price for 2027, increasing it by Rs1,000 from the rate fixed last year. According to a statement issued on Saturday, PTI Kisan Wing Central Secretary Information Khalid Nawaz Sadhraich said the announcement had come after a prolonged wait and persistent demands by farmers’ organisations, which had repeatedly urged the government to protect growers from rising production costs and financial losses. He welcomed the announcement but said its significance would depend on whether the government ensured its implementation in letter and spirit. Merely announcing a support price would serve little purpose if farmers continued to be denied the promised rate when selling their wheat, he added. Referring to previous wheat procurement seasons, Mr Sadhraich said farmers had repeatedly suffered despite government claims and official announcements regarding support prices. “In the absence of an effective procurement mechanism, middlemen and commission agents exploited growers’ vulnerability, compelling them to sell their produce at throwaway prices, often without effective intervention by the relevant authorities,” he said. He cautioned the government against repeating these mistakes, saying farmers could not afford another season of financial uncertainty after investing heavily in seeds, fertilisers, pesticides, diesel, electricity and irrigation. “A support price announced on paper provides no meaningful relief unless farmers can actually sell their wheat at the declared rate,” he added. Mr Sadhraich demanded that the government immediately announce a clear wheat procurement policy, ensuring that it purchased wheat directly from farmers at the announced rate. He said the policy should spell out procurement arrangements and operational procedures and establish an effective monitoring mechanism to prevent exploitation by middlemen and ensure that the benefits reached genuine growers. He also called for the timely establishment of procurement centres, transparent purchasing procedures and an accessible complaints mechanism so that small and medium-sized farmers could sell their produce without unnecessary hurdles or pressure from market intermediaries. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan Railways hits panic button after repeated accidents
items.description: • Emergency declared, holidays cancelled for officers until Dec 31 • Minister orders removal of operational flaws by year-end • Says health analysis of 1,546 coaches, wagons completed • Deteriorating tracks, faulty rolling stock among causes of accidents LAHORE: In view of repeated derailments and accidents, including a recent incident near Multan that killed and injured several passengers, Pakistan Railways on Saturday declared an emergency until Dec 31, cancelling all public holidays for officers and directing them to address operational deficiencies to ensure safe passenger journeys and freight transportation across the country. “Till December 31, neither I nor the officers concerned will take rest. Until all deficiencies in passenger coaches, goods wagons, locomotives, signalling and other infrastructure are removed, no one in the operations department, including me, will be allowed to avail themselves of Saturday and Sunday as holidays. Anyone found flouting these orders will be taken to task,” Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi warned while sharing details of the emergency, which came into effect on Oct 24 (Saturday). Under the emergency, aimed at ensuring safe train operations, all kinds of leave, except medical leave, as well as public holidays, including Saturdays, Sundays and other holidays, have been cancelled for officers and officials. They have also been directed to monitor train operations in the field. Railway officers travelling to other cities on official business are required to use trains. Chief engineers of the civil and mechanical departments have been directed to submit daily reports to the ministry on matters relating to their respective departments. The head of the safety department is required to submit a daily report. “It is hereby directed that all officers of Pakistan Railways shall travel by rail for all official tours, and no air travel shall be allowed or reimbursed for official tours. Furthermore, the use of official vehicles for official tours is also not allowed,” read a letter titled “Mandatory Use of Rail Transport for Official Tours”, issued to all senior and junior officers on Saturday. The minister said all dummy (faulty or brakeless) passenger coaches and goods wagons would be removed from service by Dec 31, with all such rolling stock made fully fit for operations. “Parts for coaches, wagons and locomotives, including 36,000 brake cylinders, have started arriving. Officers have been asked to start work on an emergency basis,” the minister said, adding that he was clearing a maintenance backlog accumulated over the past 10 years. “From January next year, all faulty coaches, wagons and locomotives will be fit for operations.” The minister said he would himself travel by train (railcar) from Rawalpindi to Lahore until Dec 31. Similarly, all officers would use trains to perform their official duties. “Air travel will only be allowed for me and the officers in cases of extreme emergency,” Mr Abbasi said, warning officers to remove all deficiencies in trains by Dec 31, failing which he would have no option but to take them to task. He said the health analysis of 1,546 coaches and wagons had been completed, while the inspection of the remaining around 3,000 would be completed by Nov 10. “I have directed the officers concerned that parts which can be manufactured locally should be produced at our workshops. Similarly, I have also directed the officers to meet the demand for concrete and wooden sleepers by Nov 30,” he explained. Several train accidents and derailments have been reported in recent months, including seven in July alone. The major issues identified as causes of derailments and accidents included deteriorating railway tracks, the use of dummy coaches and wagons, the manual point system (kanta system), human error, inadequate maintenance, and a lack of sufficient resources. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: PME marocaines : un potentiel de 22 milliards $ selon Expothon 2026
items.description: Le Maroc se classe au 34e rang mondial dans le « National SME Mobilization Global Index » d’Expothon Worldwide 2026, qui couvre 100 pays. Le classement recense 1,5 million de petites et moyennes entreprises dans le Royaume, dont 300.000 sont identifiées comme présentant un fort potentiel. Selon les projections de l’organisation, leur mobilisation pourrait générer jusqu’à 22 milliards de dollars de PIB additionnel. Le classement établi par l’organisation canadienne place le Maroc dans le premier tiers des économies étudiées. À l’échelle arabe, le Royaume occupe le quatrième rang. L’Égypte arrive en tête de ce groupe, au 14e rang mondial, avec 8 millions de PME, dont 1,6 million considérées comme présentant un fort potentiel. Elle est suivie par l’Arabie saoudite, 25e, qui compte 3,5 millions de PME, dont 700.000 à fort potentiel. Les Émirats arabes unis complètent le podium régional avec 1,6 million de PME, dont 320.000 à fort potentiel. Pour le Maroc, le classement fait ressortir un vivier de 300.000 entreprises considérées comme susceptibles de jouer un rôle accru dans la création de valeur. Expothon estime par ailleurs que 60.000 d’entre elles pourraient être « mobilisées », avec à la clé un potentiel de 22 milliards de dollars de PIB additionnel. Cette approche repose sur l’idée que la puissance économique d’une nation ne dépend pas uniquement de quelques grandes entreprises ou de l’afflux d’investissements étrangers, mais également de la capacité à faire émerger et grandir un tissu dense de PME. Expothon considère ainsi que l’identification des entreprises à fort potentiel, associée à des programmes structurés de formation et à l’utilisation d’outils d’intelligence artificielle, peut permettre d’accélérer leur développement. L’organisation canadienne insiste notamment sur la capacité d’adaptation des PME, qu’elle décrit comme des structures dynamiques, en évolution permanente et moins compatibles avec les mécanismes rigides de planification bureaucratique. Leur potentiel pourrait être davantage exploité grâce à un accès continu à l’expertise, aux connaissances internationales et aux technologies. L’intelligence artificielle constitue, dans cette perspective, un facteur d’accélération. Selon Expothon, les avancées technologiques permettent aujourd’hui aux petites entreprises d’accéder à des outils et à des connaissances qui étaient autrefois réservés aux grandes multinationales moyennant des investissements considérables. L’IA peut ainsi fournir directement aux entrepreneurs des informations, des bonnes pratiques et des capacités d’accompagnement à une échelle auparavant difficilement accessible. Expothon estime également que les dispositifs traditionnels de financement restent davantage adaptés aux infrastructures et aux grands projets qu’à l’accompagnement quotidien d’un vaste tissu de petites entreprises. L’enjeu consiste donc, selon l’organisation, à mettre en place des mécanismes capables d’accompagner les entrepreneurs de manière continue, plutôt que de limiter le soutien à des projets ponctuels. Dans cette logique, le classement considère les PME à fort potentiel comme un levier de création de valeur, d’innovation et d’ouverture de nouveaux marchés. Lorsqu’elles disposent d’un accès durable à l’expertise et aux technologies, ces entreprises peuvent améliorer leurs produits, accroître leur capacité de production, conquérir de nouveaux débouchés et développer leurs exportations. Le classement place l’Inde en tête du palmarès mondial avec 65 millions de PME, devant la Chine avec 50 millions et les États-Unis avec 36 millions. L’Indonésie, le Brésil, le Japon, la Russie, le Mexique, l’Allemagne et la Turquie complètent le Top 10. items.title: Stakeholders see monetary tightening tomorrow
items.description: KARACHI: Amid inflationary pressure from costly oil imports linked to the Middle East conflict, economic stakeholders have called for a 50- to 100-basis-point hike in interest rates to curb inflation. The State Bank of Pakistan’s (SBP) Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled to meet on Monday, while the financial market is filled with speculation. However, it was observed that most of the financial experts believe a 50bps hike in the interest rate is imminent. The SBP’s policy rate is 11.5 per cent. Analysts and bankers said the central bank appears to be caught between a rate hike and the long-awaited breakthrough in economic growth. “I am sure of a 50bps increase in the interest rate, but the market requires a 100bps hike to tame rising inflation,” said Rashid Masood Alam, a senior banker. Bankers say 100bps hike needed to tame inflation as Middle East conflict drives up oil import costs He said the looming US attacks on Iran are another factor that may push inflation higher and prompt the central bank to deliver a rate hike. In the first quarter of FY27, CPI inflation stood at 10.2pc, up from 4.3pc in the same period last year. “A 50bps hike looks like the sensible middle ground. Enough to acknowledge the changing risks, without unnecessarily damaging growth,” said Faisal Mamsa, CEO of Tresmark. A 50bps hike may help preserve confidence and monetary stability but the longer-term challenge is considerably bigger, he said, adding that a100bps hike would increase borrowing costs for the government and private sector, with limited additional benefit over a measured 50bps increase. All key central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India, have raised interest rates, while the IMF expects global inflation to reach 4.7pc in 2026, with a 4.1pc projection for 2027. Inflation is proving harder to contain than previously expected. Experts said the government has decided to pursue growth after achieving sustainability, but many factors are against this approach. The primary concern is the escalating war in the region, rising oil prices, and serious problems for both exports and imports as shipping costs reach their peak. A larger hike would make borrowing and investment even more difficult. “Pakistan has become better at maintaining stability, but we also need to find a way to grow without losing it,” said Mr Mamsa. At the same time, the industry is on the other side, demanding a cut in interest rates to bolster economic activity. “Raising interest rates merely in the name of controlling inflation would not prove effective in any way and would turn out to be a failed measure, the burden of which is always borne by traders and industrialists,” said Pakistan Chemicals and Dyes Merchants Association Chairman Saleem Mukati. Korangi Association of Trade and Industry and SITE Association of Industry also demanded that the interest rate be brought down to single digits. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026

items.title: Veto power hinders efforts to end conflicts: UN
items.description: • Says geopolitical fragmentation rises as major powers vie for influence • Calls for stronger cooperation on debt, technology, development ISLAMABAD: A new United Nations report has warned that the veto power of the five permanent members of the Security Council is one of the reasons multilateral mechanisms have been unable to prevent or stop the growing number of state-based conflicts. The resulting paralysis has weakened decision-making processes, prompting the UN secretary-general to call for Security Council reforms, including an expansion of its membership to ensure fairer representation, particularly for Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Asia-Pacific region. All these voices are underrepresented despite bearing much of the burden of peacemaking in an increasingly multipolar world. The ‘World Social Report 2026’ says geopolitical fragmentation has considerably heightened global risks, with multiple centres of power competing for economic, military and political dominance. According to the report, the number of countries exercising substantial influence in another country has risen from six in the 1970s to 34 today. The rise in geopolitical fragmentation is also evident from the neighbouring countries relations indicator, which has substantially deteriorated since 2008, with 59 countries recording poor ties with neighbours in 2024-25, while only 19 improved. The evolving global order demonstrates a change from two competing countries (like the bipolar world during the Cold War) to a multipolar economic, military and political power structure. In theory, a more multipolar world could strengthen multilateralism, compared to a world order dominated by two competing countries or one superpower. However, the current geopolitical fragmentation and pursuit of strategic dominance risk undermining multilateral processes and global collective actions, giving rise to “minilateralism” or “coalitions of the willing”, the report says. Accelerating climate change, rapid technological advancements and geopolitical fragmentation demand a new generation of development planning that places social inclusion at the centre of economic, digital and energy transformations. The report, prepared by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (DESA), says the experience of multilateral cooperation demonstrates that collective action can mobilise resources, strengthen accountability, support social progress, and expand opportunities for development. Renewed international cooperation is therefore essential to addressing structural constraints that exceed national capacities, including debt burdens, financing gaps, digital taxation challenges, technological divides and climate-related vulnerabilities. The report suggests that a renewed multilateral agenda should focus on three priorities. First, expanding fiscal space for social investment through stronger international tax cooperation, improved domestic resource mobilisation, and comprehensive and systematic support for developing countries to reduce the cost of capital and debt service burden. Second, promoting wider access to technology, innovation and digital infrastructure so that developing countries can participate more effectively in the global economy. Third, reforming global governance arrangements to make them more representative, inclusive and responsive to contemporary challenges, thereby restoring confidence in collective action and strengthening accountability to development outcomes. Rising conflicts and geopolitical tensions are weakening international cooperation, disrupting trade and supply chains, and diverting financial and political resources away from development priorities. Not surprisingly, military expenditures are also rising sharply: more than half of countries increased defence spending as a share of GDP between 2020 and 2024, and all nine nuclear-armed states have expanded their arsenals since 2022. As multilateral coordination becomes more difficult, countries with limited fiscal and institutional capacity face growing obstacles in accessing the financing, technology and knowledge needed for digital transformation, climate action and poverty reduction. In low-income and vulnerable economies affected by conflict and fragility, including least developed countries, these are not background conditions but direct constraints on both transformation and inclusion: conflict destroys productive assets, deters investment and weakens institutions, while displacement disrupts education, health services and livelihoods. The report stresses that although economic, digital and energy transformations are reshaping the world at an extraordinary pace, billions of people remain excluded from the jobs, skills, services, infrastructure and social protections needed to benefit from these changes. Published in Dawn, October 25th, 2026
